title: Existence of a single perfect generator
statement: For every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X [def-pc-scheme], there exists a perfect complex M in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] that is a generator in the sense of [def-pc-generators], and such that the smallest localizing, retract-closed full subcategory containing M is all of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X).

source.place: Tag 09IS (perfect-remark-perfect-generator), existence of a single perfect generator

proof.text: For an affine scheme X = Spec(A), O_X is a perfect object of D_QCoh(O_X) and a perfect generator: E = 0 exactly when Hom(O_X[n], E) vanishes for every n.

Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated with X = U union V, U quasi-compact open and V affine open, and let P be a perfect generator of D_QCoh(O_U). The cited induction step gives a perfect Q on X and a perfect Koszul object K' supported on V minus U such that Q direct-sum K' is a generator of D_QCoh(O_X); a direct sum of two perfect objects is perfect (on a common refinement of the two coverings the sum of two strictly perfect complexes is strictly perfect), and Q direct-sum K' lies in D_QCoh(O_X) because a perfect object has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves (elementary: locally it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules, whose cohomology sheaves are kernels modulo images of maps of quasi-coherent modules, hence quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherence is local). So D_QCoh(O_X) has a single perfect generator lying in D_QCoh(O_X).

For the qcqs scheme X, let P(W) be the property that D_QCoh(O_W) has a perfect generator, i.e. a perfect object G with E = 0 if and only if Hom(G[n], E) = 0 for all n, for every E in D_QCoh(O_W). P holds for every affine open by Step 1. If U is quasi-compact open, V affine open and P(U) holds, then U union V is a quasi-compact open of the quasi-separated X, hence itself quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and Step 2 applied to U union V gives P(U union V). By the induction principle, P(X) holds: D_QCoh(O_X) has a perfect generator G.

Let G be the perfect generator from Step 3 and let S be the smallest strictly full subcategory containing G and closed under shifts, cones, retracts and set-indexed direct sums. The category D_QCoh(O_X) is a triangulated subcategory of D(O_X) (elementary: it is closed under shifts, and under cones by the long exact cohomology sequence and the fact that quasi-coherent modules form a weak Serre subcategory, i.e. are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions) and has set-indexed direct sums, G, which lies in D_QCoh(O_X) by Steps 1 and 2, is compact, and the one-member family (G) has coproduct G, which is a generator. By the homotopy-colimit construction for a set of compact generators, every object Y is obtained from coproducts of shifts of G by successive cones and a final coproduct cone. Shifts of G are perfect, so the closure properties put every such object in S; hence S is all of D_QCoh(O_X).

lean.statement: theorem exists_perfect_generator (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] : ∃ P : schemeDerivedCategory X, Scheme.IsPerfect X P ∧ schemeDerivedQCohProperty X P ∧ (∀ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, IsZero E.obj ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj)) ∧ ∀ Q : ObjectProperty (schemeDerivedCategory X), Q.IsTriangulated → Q.IsStableUnderRetracts → (∀ I : Type u, Q.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)) → Q P → ∀ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, Q E.obj
